intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
Saturday morning finishes what Thursday night started. Klein Cain leads Klein Collins **14–7** in the second quarter of a first-place showdown at Klein Memorial Stadium, play resuming at **10:00 AM** after weather postponed Thursday's game. The Tigers sit **3–0 in District 15-6A** at **4–1** overall and the Hurricanes **2–0** in the district at **4–0**. A Collins win keeps the Tigers alone in first place; a Cain win pulls the Hurricanes even with Klein atop the district. Klein stayed perfect Saturday night, holding off Magnolia **28–21** to reach **5–0**.

Cain arrives off its most complete performance of the season, a **58–7** rout at Magnolia West that was **41–0** by halftime. The Hurricanes are averaging **50 points** per game through four weeks.

DCTF's computer has Collins **No. 37** and Cain **No. 49**, and the model picks the Tigers **by 8** on Cain's home field. *An unbeaten home team as an eight-point underdog? We'll see about that Saturday morning.*

The voters like Cain more than the computer does. Dave Campbell's put the Hurricanes at **No. 25** in this week's Class 6A state poll, the program's first top-25 spot of the season, after the 58-7 rout at Magnolia West. *Still an underdog Saturday morning. Just a ranked one.*

Collins is led by **Adrian Mitchell**, in his ninth season with playoff berths in all eight and regional semifinal trips each of the last two years. The Tigers arrive with momentum: Texas HS Football named Collins its Week 4 6A Team of the Week after a **42–35** comeback win at Magnolia, sealed by **Brylon Jefferson's** 48-yard touchdown pass to **Tylan Penright** with just over a minute left. The Tigers followed that with a **49–0** shutout of Klein Forest on Friday night. James Clancy's Hurricanes counter with an offense that has topped 40 points in all four games.

The postseason picture is coming into focus, too. The top four teams in District 15-6A advance to the playoffs, and the Hurricanes hold **third place** at 2–0 in district play. The field then splits by enrollment: the two qualifiers with the largest enrollments land in **Division I**, each division playing for its own state title. At **3,784 students**, Cain is the district's largest school, so a playoff-bound Cain team is headed for Division I. Win Saturday morning and the Hurricanes are tied for first.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks pilots an offense averaging 50 points a game. The junior has thrown eight touchdown passes with a 130.1 quarterback rating and 65.0 percent completions, and his legs are a weapon too: 73.5 rushing yards per game with four rushing scores. Friday's 30-yard touchdown run capped a 41–0 first half at Magnolia West.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson leads Cain at 120.8 rushing yards per game with nine total touchdowns, eight on the ground. He opened the second half Friday with a 59-yard touchdown run up the middle, and the senior has scored in every phase of this 4–0 start.

players.name: Cooper Karns
players.copy: Karns leads Cain's receivers at 83.0 yards per game. The senior turned a short throw into a 45-yard touchdown against Magnolia West, breaking a tackle and taking it the distance on a night Cain scored 58.

players.name: Easton Mizell
players.copy: Mizell leads the Hurricanes in tackles at 7.5 per game and in interceptions with two. His 43-yard pick-six just before halftime Friday turned a rout into a statement, and the junior safety is the tone-setter for a defense allowing 26.5 points a game.

players.name: Brylon Jefferson
players.copy: Jefferson leads the Tigers with nine touchdown passes, a 68.1% completion rate and a 144.5 quarterback rating. When Magnolia had Collins down 35-28, he tied it with a 31-yard touchdown run, then won it with a 48-yard strike to Tylan Penright with 1:09 left.

players.name: Tyce Hudson
players.copy: Hudson is one of the Tigers' key senior weapons: 58.4 rushing yards a game, 66.8 receiving, and a team-high nine total touchdowns. He found the end zone in the Magnolia comeback and gives Collins a back who can hurt Cain between the tackles or split wide.

players.name: Tylan Penright
players.copy: Penright leads Collins at 70.5 receiving yards a game with three touchdown catches, and he owns the biggest catch of the Tigers' season: the 48-yard touchdown from Jefferson that beat Magnolia with 1:09 to play.

players.name: Jayden Guillory
players.copy: Guillory made his mark against Magnolia with 11 tackles and a pick-six. The sophomore gives Cain another player to track in a Tiger secondary that can change the game.

recruiting.heading: Klein Collins recruiting notes
recruiting.note: A roster-wide check of the 2026 MaxPreps varsity list, On3's Klein Collins roster page and 247Sports found no verified college commitments and no top-10 position or top-100 national rankings on the current roster as of Sept. 27. Reported offers are not commitments.

items.title: Protect the quarterback
items.body: Cain's offense runs through **Jace Hanks (#9)**, and Collins will scheme to slow down a unit averaging **50 points** a game. Give Hanks time to throw and room to create, and the Tigers have to defend every weapon the Hurricanes bring.

items.title: Keep the ground game rolling
items.body: Johnson (120.8 yards a game) and Hanks (73.5) are the engine. If Collins loads the box to stop the run, Karns and Smith get room outside, and Cain's receivers have won those matchups all season.

items.title: Take it away
items.body: Cain's defense forced turnovers all night Friday: Jerod Spraberry's interception set up the opening score, Mizell's pick-six broke it open, and Reggie Yarbough added another pick. Against a 4–1 Collins team, extra possessions decide first place.

items.title: Win the wet ball
items.body: Thursday night's storms proved the point. If Saturday morning brings more wet weather, the team that protects the football protects the lead.

final.headline: Klein Collins Rallies Past Klein Cain, 40–24, to Stay Alone in First
final.byline: Cain Game Day desk · Updated Oct 3, 2026
final.body:
**Klein Collins Rallies Past Klein Cain, 40–24, to Stay Alone in First**

CAIN GAME DAY DESK · UPDATED 12:30 PM CT

Saturday morning finished what Thursday night started, and it finished with Klein Collins alone in first place.

The Tigers scored **33 points** after play resumed and beat Klein Cain **40–24** Saturday at Klein Memorial Stadium, erasing the 14–7 deficit they faced when weather postponed Thursday's game in the second quarter. Collins improved to **5–1** overall and **4–0** in District 15-6A. The Hurricanes fell to **4–1** and **2–1** in district play.

Cain led **24–14** at halftime Saturday. Collins outscored the Hurricanes **26–0** after the break. Dave Campbell's had picked the Tigers by 8. They won by 16.

**Thursday night: the 14–7 start**

Cain's opening drive stalled on fourth down after **Tyson Freeman (#17)** made a five-yard catch on third-and-8, and the punt sailed into the end zone. Collins struck first on a long **Brylon Jefferson (#18)** touchdown pass to **Tylan Penright (#14)**, and the extra point made it 7–0 Tigers.

**Eyan Johnson (#16)** answered immediately, returning the ensuing kickoff **80 yards** for a touchdown to tie it at 7–7. Asked afterward when he knew he was gone, Johnson said: *"I knew as soon as the ball touched my hands!"*

Cain took the lead in the second quarter. **Jace Hanks (#9)** ripped off a 23-yard keeper, **Israel Smith (#8)** caught a pass and carried it 20 yards to the 3, and **Earl Oguinn Jr. (#1)** scored from a direct snap. The extra point made it 14–7.

The defense did its part before the sky opened. **Jaemin Gilstrap (#42)** dropped a runner for a six-yard loss, and **Michael Rhodes Jr. (#49)** recorded a strip-sack that Collins managed to recover. Hanks added a 15-yard run and **Cooper Karns (#10)** took a catch-and-run to the Collins 15 before the weather delay ended the night.

**Saturday morning: Cain stretches it to 24–14**

Play resumed at **10:00 AM** with 9:45 left in the second quarter and Cain facing first-and-goal. Collins kept the Hurricanes out of the end zone, but **Sage DesAutels (#4)** drilled a **22-yard** field goal to make it 17–7.

Collins answered with its best drive of the half. **Easton Mizell (#47)** broke up a pass and **Lovell Christian (#45)** recorded a tackle for loss, but on third-and-long Penright hauled in a **40-yard** catch-and-run, **Demarcus Jones** added a 20-yard run on third-and-9, and Jefferson finished it with a touchdown run up the middle. The extra point cut it to 17–14 with 2:50 left in the half.

After a 20-yard screen to Karns, a 35-yard screen to Oguinn, an intentional grounding flag and a false start, Cain faced second-and-25 from its own 42. Hanks escaped a near-sack, somehow got loose and ran for the first down.

Two Oguinn runs of five yards each moved the chains again, and on first-and-goal from the 9, Hanks tucked it and scored at the right pylon. The extra point made it **24–14**.

Penright's big kickoff return gave Collins one last shot from the Cain 18. **Jaiden Pacheco (#28)** sacked Jefferson, the Tigers stalled, and with 12 seconds left Aldridge shanked a field-goal attempt. Halftime: Cain 24, Collins 14.

**Second half: all Tigers**

Collins took the second-half kickoff at its 20 and marched. **Harmon (#6)** carried the load, Penright made a contested grab over tight coverage from **Michael Elhindi (#2)**, and even with Gilstrap repeatedly disrupting the backfield and forcing two holding penalties, Jefferson found **#1** for the touchdown. The extra point made it 24–21 with 8:02 left in the third.

Cain's next drive stalled at its own 34, and after the punt Collins struck again. Harmon broke loose for a touchdown run of about **50 yards**, putting the Tigers ahead 28–24 with 5:18 left in the quarter.

Cain punted again, but the Hurricane defense kept swinging. Gilstrap's pressure helped force an incompletion on third down, and Collins eventually punted into the end zone on fourth-and-11. Karns' slant on third-and-10 moved the chains to end the quarter with Cain at its own 31, trailing 28–24.

The fourth quarter belonged to Jefferson and the Collins offense. After another Cain punt, an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on the Hurricanes gave the Tigers an automatic first down. Harmon followed with a 25-yard keeper, Jefferson ran for another first down, and Jefferson eventually scored on a sneak from the 1.

The extra point was **blocked**, leaving Collins ahead 34–24 with 7:41 left. Pacheco was shaken up during the drive but walked off under his own power.

Hanks was intercepted under pressure down the right sideline, giving Collins the ball at the Cain 21. Penright moved the Tigers to the 11, Christian recorded another tackle for loss and Mizell blew up a Harmon keeper before Jefferson found Penright on fourth down from the 14 for another touchdown.

Rhodes blocked his second extra point of the game, keeping it 40–24 with 3:46 to play.

Freeman added an 18-yard catch on Cain's next possession, but Hanks was intercepted again at midfield with 3:31 left. Collins tried to close it out on the ground, but Cain's defense produced one last stand. Mizell stuffed Jefferson on third-and-4, and Hudson was stopped on fourth-and-3.

Cain got the ball back with 1:40 left. Hanks scrambled for **30 yards** plus a 15-yard late-hit penalty, moving the Hurricanes to the Collins 34. Karns added a 15-yard catch on third-and-long, but fourth-and-5 fell incomplete with 37 seconds left.

Collins kneeled it out.

**The defense deserves its due**

The scoreboard says 40–24, but the Hurricane defense made plenty of plays in a hard-fought loss. Gilstrap spent much of the game disrupting the Collins backfield, forcing holding penalties and hurrying throws. Christian recorded multiple tackles for loss, while Mizell broke up a pass, blew up a keeper and helped produce the final fourth-down stand.

Rhodes blocked **two** extra points and added Thursday's strip-sack. Elhindi delivered a big breakup on Penright, and Pacheco's sack helped force the missed field goal at the end of the first half.

*Even after Collins took control, Cain's defense kept competing through the final possession.*

**What's next**

There isn't much time to dwell on this one. Cain travels Thursday to face unbeaten **Klein (5–0)**, which held off Magnolia 28–21 Friday night to stay perfect.

Kickoff is **7:00 PM CT** on Thursday, Oct. 8. The Hurricanes enter the week 4–1 overall and 2–1 in District 15-6A, looking to answer their first loss of the season on the road.
